issues.legal_issue: A tenant of open land on which the tenant erected a permanent structure with the landlord’s consent may claim eviction protection under the amended rent law in an eviction proceeding pending when the protection took effect, subject to the statutory rent-and-cost conditions.
material_facts: The High Court found that the tenancy was of an open site and that the tenant had erected the construction at the tenant’s own expense with the landlord’s consent.
The tenant’s appeal was pending when the provision extending protection to qualifying open-land tenants took effect.
The tenant applied within the prescribed period and unconditionally offered to pay the enhanced rent determined under the statutory formula.
issues.conclusion: The tenant qualified for the protection, subject to payment of the enhanced rent and costs. The Court determined rent by consent and made its final order on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29A(2) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, as amended, covers land let to a tenant who, with the landlord’s consent, erected a permanent structure and incurred expenses on it. Under Section 29A(6)(a)–(d), a decree for eviction in a pending suit, appeal, or other proceeding is barred except on the grounds in Section 20(2), if the tenant makes the required timely unconditional offer, pays the enhanced rent determined by the court for the relevant period, and pays costs; on payment, the suit is to be dismissed. Section 29A(7) gives the provision overriding effect. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and case_pending_when_protection_began and open_land_was_let and landlord_consented_to_permanent_construction and tenant_made_timely_unconditional_offer and tenant_pays_determined_rent_and_costs

predicates.eviction_proceeding: The matter was an eviction suit or a proceeding arising from that suit.
predicates.case_pending_when_protection_began: The eviction proceeding remained pending when the new protection became applicable.
predicates.open_land_was_let: The landlord let open land to the tenant rather than a completed building.
predicates.landlord_consented_to_permanent_construc: The landlord consented to the tenant erecting a permanent structure on the land.
predicates.tenant_made_timely_unconditional_offer: The tenant applied within the required time and unconditionally offered to pay the enhanced rent.
predicates.tenant_pays_determined_rent_and_costs: The tenant pays the rent determined by the court for the relevant period and the required costs.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding about let open land remains pending as the protection begins, and the landlord consented to permanent construction and the tenant makes the timely unconditional offer and pays the determined rent and costs, the tenant receives eviction protection.

issues.legal_issue: A court may tailor the relief in a pending eviction appeal to balance a qualifying tenant’s statutory protection with a landlord’s demonstrated need to resume business use of part of the premises.
material_facts: The tenant qualified for protection under the amended law and agreed to pay the rent determined by the Court.
The landlord asserted serious financial difficulty and a need to re-establish a business.
The premises included a shop in a recognized business locality that the landlord could use for the landlord’s own business.
The Court considered the parties’ circumstances and the equities of the case.
issues.conclusion: The Court ordered the tenant to surrender the specified shop to the landlord for the landlord’s own business, subject to the landlord returning it if the shop was not used for that purpose. The tenant could retain the remaining premises on the rent fixed by the Court, with credit for amounts already paid, and the landlord could not evict the tenant from the remaining premises for the specified period except for the stated rent default.
issues.legal_principle: The Court recognized the tenant’s entitlement to protection under Section 29A but fashioned an order to do justice between the parties in light of their circumstances and the equities. It fixed the enhanced rent with the parties’ consent, credited payments already made, and imposed conditions on the landlord’s possession and the tenant’s continued occupation. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: eviction_appeal and tenant_qualifies_for_eviction_protection and landlord_needs_business_rehabilitation and premises_include_shop_for_landlord_business and tenant_can_retain_remaining_premises_on_rent

predicates.eviction_appeal: The matter was an appeal from an eviction proceeding.
predicates.tenant_qualifies_for_eviction_protection: The tenant met the conditions for protection against eviction.
predicates.landlord_needs_business_rehabilitation: The landlord showed a need to recover premises to re-establish the landlord’s business.
predicates.premises_include_shop_for_landlord_busin: The premises included a shop suitable for the landlord’s own business use.
predicates.tenant_can_retain_remaining_premises_on_: The tenant could continue occupying the remainder while paying the rent fixed by the Court.

issues.definition: When a qualifying tenant’s eviction appeal involves a landlord who needs a suitable shop for business and the tenant can pay rent to remain in the rest of the premises, the landlord receives the shop for business and the tenant retains the remainder subject to rent and limited eviction protection.
